title: What does VaultClawback do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of VaultClawback and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, VaultClawback lets an eligible issuer recover its issued tokens from a vault under the vault feature's rules. [1]

The reference covers trust-line tokens or MPTs where the relevant capability permits clawback. This interacts with vault accounting and differs from an ordinary holder transfer. Check issuance permissions and the specific vault. A vault wrapper does not necessarily remove issuer intervention rights or make the underlying token equivalent to XRP. [1]

The VaultClawback reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using VaultClawback, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
